name: ruflo
description_short: Multi-agent orchestration platform for AI coding assistants
description_long: Ruflo (formerly Claude Flow) transforms an AI coding assistant into a multi-agent environment. It deploys swarms of specialized agents (coding, testing, security, docs) that work in parallel with persistent memory and auto-learning knowledge graphs. Supports native MCP (Model Context Protocol) and includes observability and debugging tools. Ideal if you use Claude Code or Codex and want to move to a parallelized multi-agent workflow.

name: caveman
description_short: Prompt skill that reduces ~70% output tokens via telegraphic style
description_long: Caveman is a system prompt 'skill' that forces the AI to communicate in telegraphic caveman style — eliminating pleasantries, preambles, and unnecessary grammar. Result: ~65-75% reduction in output tokens, which lowers API costs and speeds up responses. Drop-in for Claude Code, Cursor, or any agent. Ideal if you pay per-token for LLM APIs and want to reduce costs without sacrificing code quality.

name: ollama
description_short: Run LLMs locally with a single command
description_long: Ollama is a runtime that lets you download, manage and run large language models (LLMs) directly on your local machine. It supports a wide range of models: Llama 3, Mistral, Gemma, Phi-3, CodeLlama, and dozens more. Installation is a single command, and running is as simple as 'ollama run llama3'. Includes a local REST API compatible with OpenAI (port 11434), CPU and GPU support (NVIDIA, AMD, Apple Silicon), and full offline operation once a model is downloaded.

name: aider
description_short: AI pair programming in your terminal, Git-native
description_long: Aider is an AI pair programming tool in the terminal that edits your files directly and makes automatic Git commits. It understands your codebase structure via tree-sitter and can modify multiple files simultaneously to implement complete features. Supports all major LLMs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Ollama), includes an Architect mode (2 models for complex refactoring), voice-to-code, and the ability to add images and web pages as context.

name: fabric
description_short: Modular prompt patterns framework for augmenting human capabilities
description_long: Fabric proposes a library of 'Patterns' — modular, reusable prompts created by the community to solve specific tasks: summarize an article, extract YouTube insights, write in a precise style. Patterns can be chained into complex workflows. Model-agnostic (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, local models) with CLI, GUI, and API integration. The massive library of crowdsourced patterns means you have a ready-to-use toolbox rather than writing prompts from scratch.
